reason: The text depicts Saul and the Israelite leaders as dismayed and afraid (וַיֵּחַתּוּ וַיִּרְאוּ מְאֹד) when confronted by Goliath's 40-day challenge. Despite holding leadership positions, neither Saul nor any military commander volunteers to defend their people against this threat. Instead, the passage shows a young shepherd boy (David) stepping forward with the words 'Your servant will go and fight with this Philistine' (עַבְדְּךָ יֵלֵךְ וְנִלְחַם עִם־ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי הַזֶּה). The leaders remain passive and fearful, leaving their people in distress for 40 days, only consenting to David's fight after he volunteers. This demonstrates a failure of leadership accountability—rather than taking personal responsibility to address the existential threat to their people, Saul and the commanders must be galvanized to action by a non-military outsider.
